dataset: Home inspector E&O and general liability premium reference data
notes: Published figures only. Premiums are quote-based and vary by state, revenue/inspection volume, limits, deductible, endorsements and claims history. State insurance mandates are kept in a separate dataset.

gl_per_year.note: Rounded summary of the published GL figures below (Insureon median $545; Insuranceopedia about $600; WINI $400-$1,000).

factors.text: The more inspections you perform, the more opportunities clients have to sue... By performing more inspections, you increase your exposure, and your premium will be higher.
The more your home inspection business makes in a year, the more you pay your employees, and the greater the number of inspections you perform, the higher your premium will cost.
Many providers charge as little as $50 to $300 annually per tier jump in limits.
The higher your coverage limit, the more you'll pay for your policy.
For each deductible tier, you may expect to reduce your premium price from 3 to 15 percent. For most inspectors, that's a difference of $50 to $300 annually.
Higher coverage limits and lower deductibles will typically increase premium costs.
Endorsements for services such as mold or pool/spa each increase home inspector insurance cost by one to 15 percent on top of the regular premium, on average.

Purchasing extra coverage for higher-risk services, such as mold, radon, or termite inspections, can increase your insurance premiums; ancillary services such as radon or water quality testing could also raise costs.
A home inspector with a lengthy list of previous insurance claims will likely pay more.
InterNACHI member program: up to 38% off for education, experience, software, technology, and loss-free history; vanishing deductible of $500 off each claim-free renewal.
Home inspectors with more years of experience will see lower premiums than newer businesses.
Location is a rating factor (natural-disaster exposure, crime, foot traffic). Insuranceopedia GL examples run from $670/yr (OH) to $750/yr (NY).
Inspectors with employees typically face higher costs than solo inspectors; number of employees is a rating factor.

limit_options.notes: Commercial GL may be included at no additional cost.
No prices published on the page.
